What does this PR do?

fix: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/31655

    Three-layer defense: generation (snapshot), dedicated endpoint (summary), messages serialization (message-v2)
    100KB threshold for messages API (batch returns all diffs at once) vs 1MB for per-file diff endpoints (one file at a time) — conservative at batch API to prevent frontend freeze
    Frontend guard (MAX_RECONSTRUCT_BYTES) as defense-in-depth: skip expensive content reconstruction + re-diff, fall through to fast unified-diff parser
    Pre-check file content size in snapshot before attempting Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER to avoid wasted Myers diff on large files

> > So what's the reasoning behind the 4x markup on Zen?
> 
> Its like people never dealt with contracts and suppliers?
> 
> OpenCode negotiates with DeepSeek for a discount based upon the original API Prices. They get a discount, that is their profit margin. This is a contract between OpenCode and DeepSeek.
> 
> When DeepSeek reduces the prices for their own platform by 75%, this has nothing to do with the established contract. OpenCode may not be happy about this, but they are buying a service from DeepSeek, on DeepSeek's terms.
> 
> OpenCode can go back to DeepSeek and try to renegotiate the contract but the ball is in DeepSeek court, they have the power as the supplier of the good.
> 
> I am 100% sure that OpenCode has already tried to get a better contract. That is typical business practice on sudden changes.
> 
> > I was wondering why is Zen also priced at 4x?
> 
> See above. And because OpenCode is a legal company that need to make money in a legit way.
> 
> Can they be sneakily try to connect to DeepSeek their API service and use those cheaper API directly from DeepSeek. Sure, and they can then get banned from the platform, and have their contract annulled (if found out).
> 
> This is not how legal companies work. And your still forgetting that OpenCode makes no money on this backdoor approach. They will lose money with needing tons of IPs and other tricks to bypass any detection mechanics on DeepSeeks side. So any price will always be higher then what DeepSeek offers.
> 
> Legit companies do not try to pull that stuff because it opens them up to a ton of legal issues. Not just with DeepSeek but with any other API provider, as they will not do business with you (if caught doing gray stuff).
> 
> So, as long as DeepSeek does not offer a better contractual term, OpenCode is stuck on the old contract.
> 
> Right now, DeepSeek is focused on gaining market share themselves. Even if that is at the cost of business clients. Yea, it sucks but this happens a lot in the industry where are is a high demand for a product, and the supplier of that product decided to "cut out" the middle man. As in, becomes a competitor to its own clients.
> 
> There are some less reputable companies (one come to mind with a C) that are offering DeepSeek rates, but that is because they are self hosting AND running highly quantized down DSv4pro/flash models. Think of it as adding a lot of water to a famous drink, and then selling it as the original.
> 
> OpenCode seem to not play that game, to maintain their reputation. What is better on the long run if you want to grow as a legit business. OpenCode can in theory fight this by setting up their own infrastructure and running the DS4 LLMs themselves but given that China is probably a lot cheaper with electricity/datacenter/hardware (now with Chinese Made hardware).
> 
> I hope this answers some of the questions to keep coming up. And no, i have no link with DeepSeek, OpenCode, etc ... Just somebody who has been around the block for a long time. Business dealing can be nasty, ...

If OpenCode is locked into an unfavorable contract with DeepSeek, how is OpenRouter offering DeepSeek V4 Pro at roughly direct API rates with a small markup? They're the same kind of middleman. Wouldn't they face the same contract constraint?

**Update (2026-08-12):** This issue continues to affect users. Since filing, 4 more reports have appeared: #30662, #31042, #31592, #31879 — all describing the same silent title generation failure.

Our workaround for local setups: avoid setting `agent.title.model` in project configs entirely, and rely on `small_model` with a subscription-included model (e.g., `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`). The `agent.title.model` override has no fallback chain, so a single model failure silently degrades to timestamp titles.

PR #29737 (this issue's fix) is a minimal 4-line change that replaces `Effect.ignore` with `Effect.catchCause` + warning log, making failures visible. Just rebased onto latest `dev` — all CI checks passed previously. Would appreciate a review when maintainers have time.

For the fuller solution (fallback chains), see PR #27939 by @loss-and-quick.
